name: Proto-New Ireland
notes: The ancestral dialect network of the Austronesian languages of New Ireland (Ross 1994: 554); consonant system (1), p. 556. Ross (1994: 554) leaves open whether PNI was a single proto-language or a network resynthesised from several groups that came from New Britain (Ross 1988: 261-262, 280). Glottocode blank: Glottolog's New Ireland-Northwest Solomonic linkage (newi1242) also has the Northwest Solomonic languages (decision ross1994-nodes). Ross (1994) gives no POC > PNI correspondences.

name: Proto-Lavongai/Nalik
region: Northern New Ireland, New Hanover and Tigak Islands
notes: Ross's Lavongai/Nalik network: Lavongai, Tigak, Tiang, Kara, Nalik (Ross 1994: 554, after Ross 1988: 291-292). Glottolog's Tungak-Nalik (tung1294), the same five languages.
inherit_note: 'The consonant system of Proto-Lavongai/Nalik (PLN) differs from (1) only in that PNI *mʷ has merged with *m' (p. 556).

name: Proto-Madak
notes: Ross's Madak chain: Lamasong, Madak, Barok (Ross 1994: 554). Consonant system (5), p. 557; its changes from PNI (4) are not shared by Patpatar or other New Ireland languages: *mʷ > *m, *p and *f deleted before *u and merged as *p elsewhere, *R lost in most environments, *l > *n word-finally (p. 557). Glottolog's Madak linkage (mada1284).

name: Nalik
notes: Consultants from Fisoa and Bol villages (Ross 1994: 553 n. 2). Coordinates from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Kara
notes: West-coast and east-coast dialects differ in the intervocalic rules (Ross 1994: 564). Consultants from Lemekot, Fangalava and Panemecho villages (p. 553 n. 2). Coordinates from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Tigak
region: Northern New Ireland and the Tigak Islands

name: Lavongai
notes: Ross's Lavongai, Glottolog's Tungag. Coordinates from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Patpatar
region: Southern New Ireland, south of Barok
notes: Included in Ross's (1994: 556) table (3) for comparison with PMAD; not in the Madak chain. Coordinates from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Madak
notes: Consultants from Malom, Lasiki and Kaluan villages (Ross 1994: 553 n. 2); analysis of Lee & Lee (1976, 1978). Coordinates from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Lavatbura-Lamusong
notes: Glottolog's language for Ross's Lamasong, which is its dialect Lamusong (lamu1255).

name: Lamasong
notes: Consultant from Lamasong village (Ross 1994: 553 n. 2). Glottolog's Lamusong, a dialect of Lavatbura-Lamusong.
